one_liner: Senior supervisor of a Coast Guard contracting branch buying enterprise IT and cybersecurity, signing contracts as a warranted Contracting Officer up to unlimited dollar value.
fit_summary: This GS-14 role requires 4+ years in contracting, a year at GS-13-equivalent contracting work, FAC-C Professional or DAWIA Level III certification, and 24 business-related semester hours, all by the closing date. Nothing on file shows Daniel has warranted contracting, cost/price analysis, or supervisory acquisition experience; the IEM consulting background and policy knowledge don't substitute. Daniel should apply only if the IEM role actually involved years of federal contract management, otherwise target entry-level 1102 or emergency management roles instead.
eligibility: Open to the public (U.S. citizens) under direct hire authority, so you don't need federal status, but you must meet minimum qualifications by November 5, 2026.

Positive education requirement: a bachelor's degree with at least 24 semester hours in accounting, business, finance, law, contracts, purchasing, economics, management, marketing, or related fields, with transcripts submitted at application.

At least 4 years of contracting experience, including 1 full year of specialized experience at the GS-13 level (e.g., pre-/post-award, negotiation, cost and price analysis, multi-million-dollar contracts); education cannot substitute.
FAC-C Professional or DAWIA Level III equivalent certification is required, plus the ability to sit for a warrant board for an unlimited warrant.
The posting lists a Q Access Authorization and requires a DHS background investigation; you must also pass the USA Hire assessment cut score.
strategy: Before investing time, honestly check the gates: count your contracting years, confirm your 24 business credit hours on transcripts, and confirm whether you hold FAC-C Professional or DAWIA Level III. If any is missing, skip this one.

If your IEM role involved government contracts, frame it in procurement terms such as proposal pricing, contract administration, modifications, deliverable tracking, and compliance with FAR/client requirements, citing dollar values and contract types only if true.
Keep the two-page resume tight: for each job list dates, hours per week, and two to four bullets in your own words that show GS-13-level contracting work. Copied announcement text is disqualified.
Answer the questionnaire conservatively and consistently with the resume, since overstating can remove you, and prepare for the USA Hire timed assessment.
Upload unofficial transcripts and your certification document by the November 5, 2026 closing date. The window is only 10 days.
As a realistic alternative, search USAJOBS for GS-1102-07/09 contract specialist trainee or FEMA/emergency management roles where your IEM experience is directly relevant.
resume_bullets: Managed [number] [contract type, e.g., FFP/T&M] contracts valued at $[amount] for [government client], handling [modifications/option exercises/deliverable acceptance] in compliance with [FAR/client requirements].
Performed cost and price analysis for [number] proposals totaling $[amount] supporting [emergency management/disaster recovery program], and led negotiations that [describe actual outcome].
Supervised [number] staff on [contracting/program] work, assigning workload, setting priorities, and conducting [performance reviews/training] [hours per week: X].
interview_questions: Walk us through a complex, high-dollar acquisition you managed from requirement through closeout.
How do you set workload priorities and handle a subordinate whose contract files repeatedly have errors?
Describe a negotiation where you used cost or price analysis to reach a fair and reasonable price.
How would you brief senior leadership on a high-visibility protest or politically sensitive procurement?
watch_outs: Hard minimums (4 years of contracting, FAC-C/DAWIA III, 24 business credits) are likely unmet based on what's on file, and they must be met by closing.
Q Access Authorization and a DHS background investigation are required.
The position is fully on-site in Alexandria with no telework, which means a daily commute from Manassas.
The 10-day application window (Oct 26–Nov 5, 2026) is short and requires transcripts and certification uploads.
